get.description: Current tenancy mode, for the dashboard's SettingsPage (Phase 3).

Server-side admin/security audit log.

Requires admin or holding_admin. Returns the most recent events from
`user_audit_logs` with actor username resolved from the users table.

Mandates the caller's Global Context Switcher (TopNavigation's
MandateIndicator) can narrow into.

holding_admin/holding_viewer: every mandate in the holding — the same
set `GET /mandants` returns for a holding_admin, but this is also the
first endpoint holding_viewer itself can call for this purpose (`GET
/mandants` is holding_admin-strict), closing a previously-documented
gap (.plan.md) as a side effect of building this for group roles.

group_admin/group_viewer (Phase 6b / ADR-004): only their own subtree
— their own mandate (their permanent ``auth.user.mandant_id``,
guaranteed non-null whenever either role is set — see
get_auth_context()) plus every descendant in `mandant_ancestry`, which
already includes a depth-0 self-row, so this query needs no separate
"include myself" special case.

Reads ``auth.user.holding_role``/``auth.user.mandant_id`` — the
caller's permanent role/mandate — not the request's possibly-narrowed
``auth.is_holding_admin``/``auth.mandant_id``, so this list stays the
full set the caller could switch to even while currently narrowed into
one of them (see require_switch_role above). Safe to do unconditionally
here: unlike RLS-governed tables, `mandants`/`mandant_ancestry` carry no
row-level security at all, so this is a pure Python-level read with no
RLS-bypass implications either way.

Aggregated run/score counts for *mandant_id* plus every descendant
mandate (Phase 6a). See MandantRollupOut's docstring for why this needs
no RLS-shaped reasoning at all.

Phase 6b / ADR-004 — now reads the `mandant_ancestry` closure table
instead of walking `parent_id` with a recursive CTE on every call,
exactly the optimization the ADR's own "Positive consequences" section
flagged as available once that table exists: an indexed join, not a
tree walk, per request.

The caller's own mandate — any authenticated user, no holding_admin
gate. `GET /mandants` deliberately can't serve this: an ordinary
mandate-scoped user has only their own `mandant_id` (a bare UUID) on
their own UserOut, with nothing to resolve it to a display name, and
the full mandant list is holding_admin-only by design (Phase 3.2).
Returns null for a holding-only account (no personal mandate) or in
single_tenant mode.

get.description:
Initiate OIDC Authorization Code flow — redirects to the configured IdP.

ADR-005: ``?mandant=<slug>`` prefers that mandate's own per-mandant
OIDC config, falling back to the instance-wide default if none
exists. Omitting it reproduces pre-ADR-005 behaviour exactly.
Handle OIDC callback — exchange code, provision user, issue JWT, redirect to frontend.

post.description:
Rotate a refresh token: revoke the presented one, issue a fresh one.

If a revoked token is presented it indicates a replay attack — every token
in the same family is immediately revoked, forcing re-authentication on all
devices that shared this token chain.

The token comes from the request body (CLI/CI) or, when absent, from the
HttpOnly ``wombat_refresh`` cookie (dashboard).
SAML2 Assertion Consumer Service — validate IdP response and issue JWT.

get.description:
Initiate SAML2 SP-initiated SSO.

ADR-005: ``?mandant=<slug>`` prefers that mandate's own per-mandant
SAML2 config, falling back to the instance-wide default otherwise.
The resolved row's own mandate — which may be the default even when
a mandate was requested, if no override exists for it — is signed
into RelayState (same convention as OIDC's `state`) so `saml_acs`
uses the exact same row, not a fresh/possibly different resolution.

Return SP metadata XML for registering with the IdP.

ADR-005: ``?mandant=<slug>`` returns the per-mandant override's own
SP metadata (its own entity id / ACS URL / cert) if one is
configured, falling back to the instance-wide default otherwise —
an IdP admin registering a dedicated SAML app for one mandate needs
that mandate's metadata, not the shared one.

delete.description:
Delete a project and all its runs and related data.

Scoped to ``auth.mandant_id`` — "the project named X" means "in the
mandate I'm currently viewing as," the same semantic ``_get_passport``
already gives every other single-item lookup in this router. Before
this fix, the `DELETE FROM runs WHERE project = ...` below had no
mandate filter in application code at all: for an ordinary RLS-scoped
user that was a no-op in effect (RLS already hid every other mandate's
rows), but a non-narrowed holding_admin calling this genuinely deleted
*every* mandate's runs for a shared project name, not just one — found
as a side effect of the project_passports composite-key fix. Narrow via
X-Mandant-Context first to target one specific mandate; a holding-only
admin with no mandate deletes nothing (``mandant_id IS NULL`` matches
no tagged run) and gets a clean 404 below, same as every other
mandate-scoped lookup.
